lines.text: Quick test. Count the people on a phone.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Don't lose count.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: How many?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Five.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And the clown? You saw him, right?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: In a real experiment, most people on a phone call never saw him.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Psychologist Ira Hyman needed a distraction nobody could miss. Then a student told him:

lines.speaker: STUDENT
lines.text: I own a unicycle.

lines.speaker: STUDENT
lines.text: ...and a clown suit.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So for one hour, the clown rode circles in the middle of campus.

lines.speaker: INTERVIEWER
lines.text: Did you see anything unusual?

lines.speaker: FRIEND
lines.text: The clown? He was amazing!

lines.speaker: HEADPHONES
lines.text: Dude, the unicycle guy!

lines.speaker: PHONE_GUY
lines.text: Sorry... what clown?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Even asked straight out, only one in four people on a call had seen him.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Here's the weird part: people listening to music noticed him.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You see, a call pulls your mind toward someone who isn't there.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So Hyman tried something sneakier. He hung dollar bills on a branch, right at head height.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Nearly everyone ducked under it.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: On a phone? Only six in a hundred stopped for the money.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Their bodies dodged it. Their minds never saw it.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You counted five phones. You saw the clown.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Did you see the money?

casting.method: 3 candidates per role, one take each on the role's own line with the narrator's lead-in as context; measured whisper words / p, f0 median + range, loudness contour range, mean-MFCC timbre distance to James and to the other roles, spectral roll-off (band-limited voices out), noise floor, clipped edges (v6_cast.py, takes/cast_r1.txt)

decisions.STUDENT: Erby over Sheldon (288 Hz, cartoon-quirky) and Nathan (204 Hz = James's median 0.2 st away): natural everyday cadence, bright nasal timbre (centroid 1.4 kHz), 2.6 st and MFCC 7.2 from James
decisions.INTERVIEWER: Nikki over Irene (clipped start, 0.2 st from Jessica) and Sarah (falling question, 0.1 st from Erby): the friendly rising question, clean floor
decisions.FRIEND: Laura over Kymmiee (band-limited: 99 % of the energy under 2.6 kHz, lo-fi) and Jessica (0.5 st from Nikki): bright, bubbly, 293 Hz, 2.3 st above Nikki
decisions.HEADPHONES: Jerry B over Brandon (noise floor -47.7 dB under -18 LUFS speech) and Will (127 Hz, 2.1 st from Jeremy on the very next line): laid-back surfer drawl, clean floor, 8 st above the phone guy
decisions.PHONE_GUY: Jeremy over Trevor (band-limited, 4.8 kHz) and Chris (closest timbre to James of all candidates, MFCC 3.6): deep (113-126 Hz), puzzled rise; 7 takes because 'clown' was heard as 'clone' in 2 of the first 4

casting.takes_per_line: >= 4 with the winner on every character line (student 4 covering both lines, interviewer 4, friend 4, headphones 4, phone guy 7)

narrator_takes: 14 chunks x 4 takes (c01-c14, 1-3 sentences each, context-linked) + retakes c06b (n08 'RODE' capitalised, 4) and c09b (n13 punctuation, 4); chosen per line by whisper (every word right, word p), clipped edges / extra sound, the end contour (questions rise), pace and f0 against the delivery intent

processing: gains only, plus clip-gain dips on single plosive bursts (5 ms window, 4 ms raised-cosine ramps, <= 1.8 dB; listed in _build.json units[].plosive_dips) and small unit trims (<= 0.9 dB) so the peak stays under -1 dBFS without a limiter; every cut is inside true silence with 8 ms fades; no stretch, no pitch shift, no EQ, no compression
words_json: words.json = caption tokens ('1 in 4', '6 in 100' as digits: {1|one} {4|four} {6|six} {100|a hundred}; 'Five.' stays a word); words_spoken.json = one entry per spoken word; phrases.json = one entry per line with speaker (N / STUDENT / INTERVIEWER / FRIEND / HEADPHONES / PHONE_GUY); word times are the ElevenLabs v4 character times (40 ms grid) snapped to true silence, first / last word of every sentence pinned to the acoustic on / off
